title: The Impact of Annotator Personas on LLM Behavior Across the Perspectivism Spectrum
measurement_description: The paper evaluated the ability of a Large Language Model to simulate the annotation behavior of different human personas for hate speech detection. One of the datasets involved personas defined by their religious identity (Muslim), measuring how well the model could adopt this perspective in its annotations compared to actual human annotators from the same group.
findings: The study found that Llama2-13B can generate 'prototypical personas' that partially represent human annotators, including those with a Muslim identity. For the HS-Brexit dataset, the persona for a 'Male Muslim migrant' mapped to control group human annotators, not the target Muslim group, indicating an imperfect and inconsistent alignment. The findings suggest the model struggles to fully embody the nuanced perspectives of specific religious identity groups, instead converging on more generalized views.
